claim: The fit guards reject a circular arc written with a negative radius as "elliptical"
The fit guards bound a zero-radius arc by a circle on its chord, so they refuse a turn the glyph could take

triage.scenario: a glyph path `M 6 12 A 0 0 0 0 1 18 12` (SVG draws a zero-radius arc as a straight line). `walk` takes `r = max(|rx|, half)` = 6 and sees a disc of radius 6 at (12, 12), so `rotationFitsInBox` and `haloFitsInBox` measure a bulge the browser never draws. A glyph that fits is reported as not fitting, and `bakeCursor`/`resolveCursor` throw a `RangeError` for any nonzero angle on it. They should bound the arc as the segment it is (its two endpoints as radius-0 discs).
triage.cause: zero radius not read as a line

claim: A sub-step angle turns a glyph that cannot rotate on the painted tier but not on the baked one
Painted cursor state keeps a stale pointer position while inactive, so a reactivated painted cursor draws at the old pointer position

triage.scenario: the hover pump writes `setPointer` only while `active()` (`hoverCursor.ts:137`), as this module's `active()` doc invites. A brush tool is active with the pointer at A; something sets a CSS override (`setOverride('none')`, e.g. hovering a handle) or the base clears, and the pointer moves to B with no `setPointer`, since nothing is painted. When the painted cursor comes back without a pointer move (the override clears on a timer or a non-key state change; `setBase` from a `<Canvas>` render after a tool change from code), `current()` returns `{ cursor, at: A }` and the ring draws at A, far from the real pointer, until the next move. `at` should be dropped when nothing is shown (so nothing draws until a fresh position), or the state should say a position is stale.
triage.cause: position kept past the period it stops being written

claim: The sink clears painted overrides it never set, unlike the element side
bakeFallback refuses -webkit- prefixed cursor keyword aliases (e.g. -webkit-grab) that Chrome accepts

triage.scenario: `cursorFor('pencil', { fallback: '-webkit-grab' })`, or `{ fallback: 'image-set("a.png" 1x, "a@2x.png" 2x) 4 4, default' }`, throws `RangeError: cursor fallback … is not a cursor value`. Chrome parses both: it keeps `-webkit-grab`/`-webkit-grabbing`/`-webkit-zoom-in`/`-webkit-zoom-out` as aliases, and `image-set()`/`-webkit-image-set()` are valid `<cursor-image>` entries. The rule (docs/unruled.md, cursor audit 88) is to refuse what is *not* a cursor value, so these should pass. The `image-set` case is the more realistic one, since it is the usual way to give a bitmap cursor a retina variant.

A world-unit brush ring of radius 0 is drawn at the 24 px default, while a px ring of radius 0 is drawn at 1 px

rotationFitsInBox measures an arc by its bounding square's corners, rejecting arcs that fit at every angle

bakeFallback accepts fallbacks that make the browser drop the whole declaration
`brushRing(r, 'world')` with r = 0 draws a 24 px baked ring, while `brushRing(0, 'px')` draws a 1 px ring
`bakeFallback` refuses valid cursor lists whose images are `image-set(…)` or whose hotspot uses an exponent or `+`
An invalid `fallback` throws on the CSS tier but is accepted when the same spec resolves painted
The fit guards' path walk accepts absolute H, V, C, Q, S and T without throwing, and mis-measures H and V
Equality check ignores fallback, so a fallback-only update is dropped: current().cursor.fallback stays stale and subscribers are not notified

triage.scenario: `setBase({ kind: 'painted', glyph: 'brush', angle: 0, worldRadius: 4, fallback: 'crosshair' })`, then `setBase({ …same…, fallback: 'default' })` (useToolCursor re-calls `setBase` when only `tier.fallback` changes, since its key includes it). `same()` compares glyph, mark, angle, size and worldRadius but not `fallback`, so the second write returns early without storing the new object, and `current().cursor.fallback` still answers `'crosshair'`. It should store the new cursor; skipping the notify is fine because nothing drawn changed. No caller in the repo reads the state's `fallback` today (the sink keeps its own copy), so the stale value only shows through the public `current()`.

claim: createCursorSink recognizes its own write by string equality with `style.cursor`, which the browser hands back serialized, so an override set and then cleared without a base can stay on the element
The arc bound uses the authored radius even when SVG scales it up, under-reporting an arc whose radius is shorter than half its chord
A marked glyph accepts an angle but is never checked for rotation, and the crosshair's marks fall outside the box when rotated
`walk` does not return the current point to the subpath start on `Z`
brushRing answers a 24 px default ring for a negative, NaN or infinite radius instead of rejecting it or drawing it at its minimum size
The fit guards measure every path's halo as half the halo width, so a stroke path's halo can leave the box unseen — and the marked crosshair's does
bakeFallback refuses a valid url(…) fallback whose unquoted URL contains a CSS escape

triage.scenario: `bakeCursor(GLYPHS.pen, { fallback: 'url(pen.png) 1e1 4, auto' })`, or `'url(pen.png) +4 +4, auto'`, or `'url(a\\(b.png), auto'` → `RangeError: cursor fallback … is not a cursor value`. Each is a valid CSS `cursor` list (a hotspot is a CSS `<number>`, which allows a sign and an exponent; an unquoted `url()` allows backslash escapes), so the browser would accept it. The hotspot pattern `-?\d*\.?\d+` and the unquoted-url class `[^\s"'()\\]*` reject them, the regex fails to consume the entry, and the remainder is not a keyword. The same validation runs in `cursorFor` and `resolveCursor`, so every tier throws.
triage.cause: hand-rolled number/url grammar narrower than CSS

claim: bakeFallback rejects valid url(…) hotspots that use a + sign, an exponent, or no space after the closing paren

triage.scenario: the hotspot grammar is `-?\d*\.?\d+` behind a mandatory `\s+`. CSS `<number>` also allows a leading `+` and an exponent, so `fallback: 'url(a.png) +4 4, default'` and `'url(a.png) 1e1 4, default'` are valid cursor values. The browser takes them, but `bakeFallback` throws `RangeError: … is not a cursor value`, which reaches `bakeCursor`, `cursorFor` and `resolveCursor` on every tier. So a fallback the doc says is accepted ("optionally after `url(…)` images of its own") throws for an ordinary spelling of the hotspot. `image-set(…)` entries, which Chrome takes in `cursor`, are refused the same way.
triage.cause: hotspot regex narrower than the CSS number grammar

claim: The bake cache's key takes any size and any fallback string, so it is unbounded despite its comment

A CursorSink cannot give the element back once setBase has been called
The pencil glyph's detail line extends past the ink and halo, so it shows as an unhaloed white stub

triage.scenario: the detail is collinear with the ink's butt edge (16,8)–(19,11) (all three points lie on y = x − 8) and overshoots the corner (16,8) by 2.83 units to (14,6). A `detail` is drawn in the halo color with no halo of its own and is meant to be "a division inside the silhouette" (types.ts). Here it straddles the outer edge, shaving 0.6 units of ink off the butt end, and its last ~1.5 units sit outside the 1.3-unit halo around that corner. On white paper that stub is invisible. On dark chrome, both tiers draw a white tick sticking out of the pencil's outline with no ink edge, because the painter and the baker share `cursorPaintOps`. It should lie inside the body, as the pen's detail `M 8.4 13.9 L 12.2 10.1` does. `haloFitsInBox` cannot catch this: the stub stays inside the box.
triage.cause: detail authored on the silhouette edge, not inside it

claim: An infinite `size` throws in bakeCursor/cursorFor but draws at 24 px through resolveCursor
An empty fallback bakes an invalid cursor declaration
resolveCursor validates glyph and mark on the CSS tier only
`brushRing(r, 'world')` with a huge finite radius is accepted, and its painted size overflows to Infinity at draw
worldCursorPx returns Infinity for a finite world radius at a large zoom

triage.scenario: `resolveCursor({ glyph: 'brush', worldRadius: 1e300 })` resolves without complaint to a painted cursor. At a view scale of 1e9, `worldRadius * scale * (box / r)` overflows to `Infinity`, and `Math.max(1, Infinity)` keeps it. A painter that feeds that size to `cursorPaintMatrix` gets infinite entries (a·0 → NaN in the translation), and `chromeLineWidthScale` gives 0. The px unit refuses an overflowing size (`brushRing` throws; ruled in cursor audit 88), so the world unit answers the same overflow a second way: it hands out a non-finite size instead of refusing or capping it.

claim: A cursor sink overwrites another writer's painted override and, on release, clears it to null instead of restoring the earlier value

triage.scenario: two writers share one `PaintedCursorState` (another sink, or code calling `painted.setOverride` directly, as `createCursorSink`'s doc says it leaves alone). Writer A sets override painted `{glyph:'brush'}`. Sink B, which does not own the base, calls `setOverride('pointer')` → writePainted sets the state's override to `'none'` and marks `ownsPaintedOverride`. B then calls `setOverride(null)` → writePainted calls `painted.setOverride(null)`. A's brush override is gone while A still believes it is set; nothing paints until A writes again. The element's style is handled the other way: `write` records `prior` and `giveBack` restores it only if unchanged since. The painted slot gets no prior and no "unchanged since" check, so the two halves of one sink answer "put back what I replaced" differently. Likewise a sink that owns the base clears any override another writer set on the state on every write (`else if (ownsBase || ownsPaintedOverride) painted.setOverride(null)`).
triage.cause: painted override slot written without recording/restoring the prior value

claim: cursorFor answers a cached cursor for an unknown glyph name instead of throwing
Changing an override puts back a stale cursor when other code wrote the element in between
Clearing an override on a sink that does not own the base erases the cursor other code had set
The fit guards bound an arc whose ends meet by a full circle the browser never draws

triage.scenario: `M 12 12 A 9 9 0 0 1 12 12`: SVG leaves an arc out entirely when its endpoints are equal. Here `half` is 0, `r` is 9 and the center is the point itself, so `walk` reports a radius-9 disc. That can push a fitting glyph out of `haloFitsInBox`/`rotationFitsInBox`, and a turn on it throws. The arc should add nothing past its endpoint.

claim: A px-unit brushRing draws its ring line thicker as the radius grows, while the same ring in world units stays at chrome weight

triage.scenario: `brushRing(60, 'px')` gives `{ glyph: 'brush', size: 145 }`. That goes to the painted tier with a fixed size, and `paintedCursorLayer` passes no `lineWidthScale` for a fixed size. The 1.6-unit stroke therefore draws at 1.6 × 145 / 24 ≈ 9.7 CSS px, inside a halo about 25 px wide. Below the cap, `brushRing(20, 'px')` bakes at size 48 with a 3.2 px line. On a zoom where 60 world units come to 60 px, `brushRing(60, 'world')` draws the same ring radius with a 1.6 px line, because the layer applies `chromeLineWidthScale` to a world-sized spec. So one function gives two line weights for the same on-screen ring, depending only on the unit. A brush ring should keep chrome line weight in either unit, as `worldCursorPx` / `chromeLineWidthScale` intend for a glyph that measures something.
triage.cause: line weight scaled with size on the fixed-size path, chrome weight on the world path
